description: Poll cached messages from one or more ntfy topics with optional filters. Returns a snapshot, not a live stream — use it to confirm delivery, replay missed alerts, or audit topic activity. Multiple topics are passed as a comma-separated list. One call returns the newest messages of the window; when more match, page through the whole window oldest-first by passing `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. Long bodies are truncated client-side to keep list responses bounded; refetch with that message `id` to read one in full.

base_url.description: Override `NTFY_BASE_URL` for this call — an absolute `http(s)://` URL. Server-configured auth credentials are forwarded only when the override matches a registered server (`NTFY_BASE_URL` or an `NTFY_SERVERS` entry); otherwise the request goes out unauthenticated.

cursor.description: Continue a paged read: pass the previous response's `nextCursor` verbatim, with the same `topic`, `since`, and filters. Returns up to `limit` messages starting at that message (inclusive), oldest-first, and a new `nextCursor` while more remain. Under a duration `since` (`10m`, `2h`), the cursor also holds the window where the walk began, so later pages stay reachable after the duration's lower bound has moved past the first messages. Omit it to get the newest messages of the window.

id.description: Exact-match a single message ID. Pinning one message this way also returns its body in full — the ~500-char cap that applies to list results is lifted. `since` still bounds which cached messages are searched, so widen it when the target is older than the default window.

limit.description: Client-side cap on returned messages. Default 20; one call returns at most 100, so a larger value is served as 100. Without `cursor`, the newest `limit` of the window are returned (listed oldest-first); with `cursor`, up to `limit` starting at the cursor message. `truncated` and `nextCursor` say when more remain.

priority.description: Match any priority in the list (logical OR). Empty/omitted matches all priorities.

since.description: Lower bound of the window. Default `10m`, tighter than ntfy's default to keep the common 'did my recent notification land?' lookup cheap. Accepts a duration in seconds, minutes, or hours (`30s`, `10m`, `2h`, `24h`), a Unix timestamp, the keywords `all` (every cached message — up to ~12h on ntfy.sh) or `latest` (most recent only), or a message ID, which returns only the messages after that one — an ID ntfy no longer holds returns the whole cache rather than an error. To page through a window larger than one call returns, use `cursor`, not `since`; keep `since` the same on every page, even a duration — the cursor holds the window where the walk began.

tags.description: Match all tags in the list (logical AND). Empty/omitted matches all messages regardless of tags.

topic.description: Single topic or comma-separated list (e.g., `alerts` or `alerts,backups,phil_alerts`). Required unless `NTFY_DEFAULT_TOPIC` is set.

name: ntfy_fetch_messages

appliedFilters.description: Active filter inputs the server applied; absent when no filters were set.

id.description: Echo of the input id filter; absent when not set.

message.description: Echo of the input message filter; absent when not set.

priority.description: Echo of the input priority filter; absent when not set.

tags.description: Echo of the input tag filter; absent when not set.

title.description: Echo of the input title filter; absent when not set.

count.description: Number of messages returned in this response.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `forbidden_topic`: Auth required for the target topic. `invalid_since`: `since` value could not be parsed by ntfy (a malformed duration or timestamp, or a duration unit other than `s`, `m`, `h`). `cursor_not_found`: `cursor` names no message in the fetched window: its message expired from ntfy's cache or fell outside ntfy's replay, or the cursor came from a call with a different `topic`, `since`, or filters. `rate_limited`: ntfy answered 429 — on the status line, or as an error line written into the replay — and was still answering it when retries ran out. `upstream_unreachable`: DNS, connection, or network failure reaching the ntfy server after retries were exhausted, or no complete answer within the call deadline. `upstream_malformed`: The poll response was not ntfy's JSON message stream (an HTML page, a cut-off or corrupted body) on every attempt. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

messages.description: Cached messages matching the filters, oldest-first (chronological order from ntfy).

items.description: A single cached ntfy message envelope.

actions.description: Action buttons echoed by ntfy. Discriminated by `action`. Absent when no actions were set.

items.description: Action button echoed by ntfy. Discriminated by `action` (`view`, `broadcast`, `http`, `copy`).

oneOf.description: Open a URL or app on tap.

clear.description: Whether the notification dismisses on tap.

oneOf.description: Send an Android broadcast intent on tap.

clear.description: Whether the notification dismisses on tap.

extras.description: String extras passed alongside the broadcast.

oneOf.description: Fire an HTTP request on tap.

clear.description: Whether the notification dismisses when the request succeeds.

oneOf.description: Copy a value to the clipboard on tap.

clear.description: Whether the notification dismisses on tap.

value.description: Value copied to the device clipboard on tap.

attachment.description: Attachment metadata; absent when the message had no attachment.

expires.description: Unix seconds when the hosted attachment ages out.

type.description: Mime type — present only when ntfy hosted the upload.

click.description: Click URL; absent when no click action was set.

expires.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the message ages out of cache.

id.description: Message ID — pass back as `id` to fetch this message with its whole body, or as `sequence_id` to manage it. To page through a window, pass the `nextCursor` enrichment value as `cursor`.

markdown.description: True when the message was published as Markdown, so `message` is Markdown source; absent for plain text.

message.description: Notification body. Truncated client-side to ~500 chars; see `messageTruncated` for the count of dropped chars. Returned whole when the call pinned a single message via `id`. Absent on clear/delete events.

messageTruncated.description: Count of additional characters dropped from `message`. To read the whole body, call this tool again with `id` set to this message's `id` and a `since` window that still covers it — a single-message fetch skips truncation. Absent when the full body fit within the cap or truncation was skipped.

sequence_id.description: Present on update/clear/delete events pointing back to the original message; absent on initial publishes.

tags.description: Tags applied to the notification; absent when none.

time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when ntfy accepted the message.

title.description: Notification title; absent when no title was set.

topic.description: Topic the message was published to.

nextCursor.description: Pass verbatim as `cursor`, with the same `topic`, `since`, and filters, to get the next page oldest-first. Without `cursor` it names the oldest message of the window, starting a walk through the whole window; on a cursor page, the message after this page. Under a duration `since` it is `<message id>@<unix seconds>`, the seconds marking where the walk began, which keeps the walk's window from shrinking as ntfy's clock advances. Absent on the last page, on an empty result, and when nothing was left out.

notice.description: Guidance when the result is empty or truncated, here or by ntfy — echoes the criteria and suggests how to broaden or paginate.

since.description: Echo of the `since` value sent to ntfy — the input trimmed, or the default `10m` when it was omitted or blank. On a cursor page under a duration, the Unix time where the walk began, which the cursor carries.

topic.description: Echo of the resolved topic (or comma-separated list) — useful when `NTFY_DEFAULT_TOPIC` filled in for an omitted `topic`.

totalCount.description: Messages in the fetched window, before `limit` and `cursor` apply. On a cursor page under a duration `since`, the window runs from where the walk began, so it counts arrivals since then and drops expired messages. When `upstreamTruncated` is set it counts only what ntfy returned.

truncated.description: True when this response holds fewer messages than `totalCount`. Without `cursor`, the newest `limit` are returned and the older head is left out; on a cursor page, the other pages hold the rest. `nextCursor` says whether more follow.

upstreamTruncated.description: True when ntfy itself capped the replay at its per-topic size limit and dropped the oldest messages in the window before responding. Those messages are not reachable through this server, and every count reported covers only what ntfy returned. Absent when ntfy sent the whole window.
